# OpenSec v1 test vectors (docs/protocol/opensec.md). Hex unless noted; datagrams as sent on the wire.
#
# case <name> starts a handshake; the lines after it are its inputs, packets and derived values:
#   *_secret: X25519 private keys as 32 raw bytes (the X25519 function clamps them)
#   ee, es: the X25519 outputs (es only with SERVER_AUTH); okm: the 64 HKDF output bytes
#   confirm_tag: the last 16 bytes of the server hello
# nonce <c2s|s2c> <counter, decimal> <12-byte AEAD nonce>
# record <c2s|s2c> <counter, decimal> <plaintext> <encrypted datagram>
#
# reject-client-hello <name> <client hello>: a server must not answer it
# reject-server-hello <name> <client ephemeral secret> <client hello> <pinned key or -> <server hello>:
#   a client must fail the handshake
# window <name> <step>...: one receiver from a fresh session, fed records in order. Each step is
#   <low 32 bits on the wire, decimal>[!]=<full counter the receiver must accept, decimal, or x to drop>;
#   ! marks a record whose tag fails, which must change nothing.
